first_impression.reaction: I typed 'greece wedding packages all inclusive' on the train. By the second sentence I know what a package usually covers, and by the third I know what usually isn't in it. That's the answer. The takeaways are four lines and the second one is the thing I actually needed to hear: 'all inclusive' is the holiday, not the wedding. I'd read the takeaways, glance at the table, check the FAQ and bookmark.

journey.quote: A Greek venue package usually bundles the ceremony set-up, a coordinator and a set list of touches for the day.
journey.reaction: Second sentence and I've got my answer. No wading.

journey.quote: Where a Greek resort calls itself all inclusive, the phrase almost always describes the holiday stay rather than the wedding package.
journey.reaction: Oh. That's the catch I didn't know about. This is the line I'd remember and repeat to friends.

journey.section: What all inclusive means at a Greek wedding venue
journey.quote: None of the ten venues in this comparison sells its wedding package as all inclusive.
journey.reaction: Heading matches my question and the first line answers it bluntly. Love that.

journey.quote: **A cake and a toast.** Ikos Aria includes a cake to serve 10 people, Canaves a two-tier cake and a glass of sparkling wine for the toast, and Andronis a two-tier cake with a bottle of sparkling wine.
journey.reaction: Bold lead-ins make this easy to thumb through. I only read the bold bits and still get it.

journey.quote: | Venue and region | Package | Ceremony types | Main inclusions (short) | Charged on top or separate | Requirements or minimums |
journey.reaction: Six columns on a phone screen. I'll be scrolling sideways and losing which row I'm on. Useful, but I'd probably screenshot it and look at it later on a laptop.

journey.quote: On the day, the list runs to two witnesses if you need them, a ceremony table with a seasonal flower display, bouquet and boutonniere, rose petals, a pre-recorded ceremony playlist, champagne while you dress, a short fireworks display and flowers and petals in your room afterwards.
journey.reaction: Venue after venue of long inclusion lists in sentences. The table already gave me the summary, so I start thumbing past here.

journey.quote: Santorini Gem is a caldera venue with a wedding villa, and its [Rental Packages 2026](https://santorinigem.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/SANTORINI-GEM_RENTAL-PACKAGES_2026.pdf) sell space by the session.
journey.reaction: 2026 in the document names. So this is current, which answers my 'is this still true' worry.

journey.section: How to compare two all-inclusive quotes like for like
journey.quote: Two quotes compare only when they describe the same wedding.
journey.reaction: Short, clear rule. The question list under 'Per guest or fixed' is something I'd screenshot.

journey.section: How to compare two all-inclusive quotes like for like
journey.quote: Unused fireworks may not become extra flowers.
journey.reaction: Ha, that made it click. Memorable.

journey.section: The legal side in brief / Planning from Australia
journey.quote: From Australia, a few questions decide how a package lands in practice:
journey.reaction: Embassy in Athens, Smartraveller, now 'From Australia'. Not me, I'm in Singapore. I skip it, but I start wondering if this site is only for Australians.
Short answer first, then the detail. Exactly how an FAQ should read on a phone.

unanswered_questions: Roughly what does an all-inclusive Greek wedding cost? Even a ballpark. There's nothing on price.
Does Wedded Wonderland work with couples outside Australia, or only Australians?
If I just want the cheapest simple option for two of us, which of these ten should I look at first?

turn_offs_found.quote: | Venue and region | Package | Ceremony types | Main inclusions (short) | Charged on top or separate | Requirements or minimums |
turn_offs_found.why: A six-column table is hard to read on a phone on the train. I'd want the key columns first (venue, what's in, what's extra) or a card-style view per venue so I don't scroll sideways.

turn_offs_found.quote: On the day, the list runs to two witnesses if you need them, a ceremony table with a seasonal flower display, bouquet and boutonniere, rose petals, a pre-recorded ceremony playlist, champagne while you dress, a short fireworks display and flowers and petals in your room afterwards.
turn_offs_found.why: The venue-by-venue section is long paragraphs of item lists. After the table it feels like repetition, and I can't skim a sentence with eight items in it. A one-line 'best for' per venue would help me decide which to read.

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit
turn_offs_found.why: Coming straight after the legal and 'Planning from Australia' sections, this makes me think the service isn't for someone in Singapore, so I'm less likely to bookmark or come back.

would_share_with: My engaged friend who's been looking at Ikos for a 'wedding holiday'; I'd send her the key takeaways so she knows the wedding package is separate

cta_reaction.why: I'm only researching, I haven't got a shortlist yet. No pop-ups or walls, so no complaints, and I'd bookmark before I'd book. The AUD and Australian framing also makes me unsure they'd take me.

top_3_changes: Make the comparison table phone-friendly: trim to the three or four columns that matter most, or show each venue as a stacked card on mobile.
In 'Venue by venue', open each venue with a one-line summary (who it suits, ceremony only or with reception, key requirement) before the full inclusion list.
Phrase the AUD line in the CTA as a benefit for Australian couples rather than implying the service is only for Australians.
